papers.title_en: BUMP: Body-driven Unified Multi-object Physics for HOI Synthesis
papers.authors: Wonjung Woo, Hyeonwoo Kim, Hanbyul Joo
papers.evidence: 文本驱动的全身人体运动生成用于多物体交互
papers.tldr: 多物体人-物交互（HOI）生成困难：人体运动体现语义意图，被操作物体需与人保持协调，而周围物体主要作为接触与碰撞的物理结果而运动。BUMP 提出“学习意图运动、仿真物理后果”的文本驱动框架：先根据文本与场景生成全身人体运动，再预测少量被意图操作的驱动物体轨迹，其余响应物体交由物理仿真得到。方法融合人体运动、全身HOI与手部操作三类异构数据以缓解配对数据稀缺，并提出以结果为目标条件的交互编辑。在单物体与多物体HOI基准上均取得强劲性能。
papers.abstract_en: Generating human-object interactions (HOIs) with multiple objects is challenging because the resulting motions arise from different underlying causes. Human motion reflects semantic intent, intentionally manipulated objects must remain coordinated with the human, while surrounding objects move primarily as physical consequences of contact and collision. We present BUMP, a text-driven framework for multi-object HOI generation based on a simple principle: learn intentional motion and simulate physical consequences. Our method first generates full-body human motion from text and scene context, then predicts trajectories for a small number of intentionally manipulated driver objects conditioned on the human motion. We then obtain responder object motions through physics simulation, allowing the framework to handle varying numbers and configurations of surrounding objects without expanding the learned trajectory output space. To address the scarcity of paired full-body multi-object HOI data, we combine heterogeneous supervision from human-only motion, full-body HOI, and hand-centric manipulation data augmented with plausible body motion. We further introduce outcome-conditioned interaction editing, which infers a local modification of the causal driver object trajectory from a desired responder object behavior without requiring an explicit target driver object trajectory. Experiments demonstrate strong performance on both single-object and multi-object HOI benchmarks. Qualitative results showcase diverse scenarios involving inter-object relationships and edits, highlighting the advantage of our unified model formulation.

papers.title_en: DexGraspFlow: Topology-Aware SE(3) Flow Matching for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasp Generation
papers.authors: Bin Zhou, Boyu Ma, Xinyu Zhou, Jiahua Dong, Chuhao Zhou, Yizhou Liu, Hao Wan, Jianfei Yang
papers.evidence: 面向灵巧手姿态生成的条件SE(3)流匹配
papers.tldr: 跨具身灵巧抓取受手部几何、关节参数与运动学拓扑差异制约，仅靠link空间关系难以充分建模。DexGraspFlow提出条件式link级SE(3)流匹配，融合局部几何与运动学树距离注意力偏置，用双流DiT协调link-link与link-object交互并联合学习平移/旋转速度场。在三种手、30个对象-手对中平均仿真成功率95.33%，含逆运动学的生成延迟较SOTA降低约49%。它还支持七种去指变体零样本适应与手掌朝向控制，真机100次抓取成功率达91%。
papers.abstract_en: Differences in hand geometry, joint parameterization, and kinematic topology pose challenges for cross-embodiment dexterous grasp generation. However, spatial relations among links alone are insufficient to fully capture the hand's kinematic topology. We propose DexGraspFlow, a conditional link-level $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ flow-matching framework integrating geometric relations and kinematic topology. The framework encodes local object geometry, link geometry, and current poses. A dual-stream DiT models link--link coordination and link--object interaction, while attention biases derived from kinematic-tree distances provide explicit structural information for modeling evolving geometric interactions. The model jointly learns translational and rotational velocity fields, integrates them to generate link poses, and recovers joint configurations through inverse kinematics. Additionally, inference-time palm-orientation guidance enables controllable grasp generation without retraining. Across three robotic hands and 30 object--hand pairs, DexGraspFlow achieves a 95.33\% average simulation success rate, with an average generation latency, including inverse kinematics, approximately 49\% lower than that of a state-of-the-art baseline. Further experiments demonstrate zero-shot adaptability to seven finger-removal variants and palm-orientation control. A model trained on demonstrations for the deployed hand achieves a 91\% success rate over 100 real-robot grasping trials, supporting the framework's applicability to physical grasp execution.

papers.title_en: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
papers.authors: Noam Rotstein, Yoad Tewel, Chen Tessler, Haggai Maron, Gal Chechik, Or Litany, Yoni Kasten, Yuval Atzmon
papers.evidence: 为任意骨架联合生成三维动作与视频
papers.tldr: 视频生成模型能生成逼真运动，但难以把运动还原为可在3D场景回放、驱动任意骨架的3D动画。本文提出联合生成视频、任意rig的3D运动及配准相机的模型：将支持任意骨架的3D运动模型与预训练视频模型通过少量cross-attention连接，并用关节定位恢复相机。模型从文本忠实驱动多样rig，运动能响应场景，还支持视频转rig运动、rig运动转视频和关键帧控制。
papers.abstract_en: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place animated 3D assets in scenes suited to their actions, curating the edits so their known motion remains valid. Together with human and robot video, this yields nearly 200K training pairs. Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene. It also turns video into rig motion, rig motion into video, and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion. Videos and additional results are available on our project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/.

papers.title_en: Self-Conditioning Enables Deep Sequential Reasoning in Flow Matching
papers.authors: Zeyang Zhang, Linxiang Gao, Meiqi Gu, Xingyan Chen, Minrui Luo, Kaifeng Lyu, Tianxing He
papers.evidence: 流匹配采样器的自条件与表达能力
papers.tldr: 视觉推理可通过图像生成求解，但本文指出普通 flow matching 的多步采样未必带来更深推理。作者从电路复杂度证明其轨迹可由常数轮并行评估模拟，并提出用 self-conditioning 在采样步间传递更多信息。实验显示该方法在多种视觉推理任务上准确率更高、推理深度更大，且随采样步数增加持续提升。理论证明其可使常数深度骨干达到空间有界图灵机表达能力。
papers.abstract_en: Recent work has explored visual reasoning through image generation, where models solve visual-reasoning problems by directly generating solution images. Intuitively, iterative samplers such as flow matching are well suited to this task, since each sampling step may resemble one reasoning step. However, in this work, from a circuit complexity perspective, we show that this intuition is misleading. We prove that as long as the model outputs satisfy certain mild regularity conditions, the trajectory of the vanilla flow-matching sampler can be simulated by a constant number of sequential rounds of parallel model evaluations. Consequently, additional sampling steps cannot increase the expressive power of a constant-depth backbone model under the standard complexity-theoretic model of transformers. We then reveal that self-conditioning, which conditions the model on the previous step's estimate of the final image, plays a previously unrecognized role in removing this bottleneck. Controlled experiments on diverse visual-reasoning tasks show that flow matching with self-conditioning achieves higher accuracy and greater reasoning depth than vanilla flow matching, and its performance improves with more sampling steps. Theoretically, we prove that with self-conditioning, a constant-depth backbone can achieve expressive power equivalent to that of space-bounded Turing machines. Our study suggests a design principle for future visual reasoning research: carry more information between sampling steps, so that additional steps translate into deeper reasoning.

papers.title_en: RoPE-Flow: Monocular Vision-based Robot Pose Estimation via 2D Graph-Conditioned 3D Flow Matching
papers.authors: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Zhiwei Fang, Rulin Zhou, Quanlu Zhang, Changjing Liu, Beilei Cui, Yiming Huang, Hongliang Ren
papers.evidence: 端到端流匹配框架用于单目图像的三维结构回归
papers.tldr: 单目图像机器人位姿估计对视觉导航控制重要，但现有方法依赖耗时渲染或2D-3D配准，存在投影歧义、远端关节误差累积和关节学习不均衡。RoPE-Flow以端到端流匹配框架为核心，结合关键点中心特征提取器、图引导条件生成器与可学习邻接图，并引入骨长损失和射线深度损失及逐关节加权。多类机器人多相机实验优于现有方法，并在新建跨场景基准上展现零样本泛化。该工作为单目机器人位姿估计提供了结构一致且可泛化的新范式。
papers.abstract_en: Camera-to-robot pose estimation from a monocular image is significant for vision-based robot navigation and control. However, recovering 3D structural features from 2D observations remains a challenging task. Existing camera-to-robot pose estimation methods either rely on time-consuming iterative rendering or involve sophisticated 2D-3D registration which suffers from projection ambiguity, accumulated errors for distal joints and imbalanced learning for different joints. In this work, we propose RoPE-Flow, an end-to-end flow matching-based framework for camera-to-robot pose estimation. From the predicted 2D heatmaps, we propose a Keypoint-centered Feature Extractor to obtain positional features along with contextual representations from keypoints-centered multi-scale patches. Moreover, we introduce Graph-guided Condition Generator, which embeds a learnable adjacency map to generate condition for flow matching based on correlation among keypoints. Besides, we introduce Bone Length Loss and Ray-Depth Loss for topological consistency and scale stability, with joint-wise weighting to mitigate varied prediction difficulty across joints. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation across different types of robots with mutiple cameras. Besides, we establish a novel cross-scene benchmark to demonstrate the outstanding performance of RoPE-Flow on zero-shot cross-scene robot pose estimation. Meanwhile, animated visualizations are shown on the website: ropeflow.netlify.app

papers.title_en: FlashControl: One-Step Controllable Generator via Distillation-Friendly Single-Stream Teachers
papers.authors: Ngan Nguyen, Dung Nguyen, Quan Dao, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Minh Hoai, Cuong Pham, Anh Tran
papers.evidence: 用于可控视觉生成与蒸馏的扩散模型
papers.tldr: 扩散模型在文生图与可控生成中表现突出，但多步采样导致推理缓慢；现有一步蒸馏多聚焦文生图，ControlNet等可控模型因双分支结构难以蒸馏。本文提出DeltaControl，不增加条件分支，仅微调原模型部分层实现单流多步空间可控生成，并匹配双分支性能。进一步步蒸馏得到FlashControl，单次前向即可完成空间可控生成。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion models have become a leading approach in visual generative modeling, particularly effective in text-to-image and controllable generation. Their main drawback is slow inference as it requires many sampling steps. While recent distillation methods enable one-step text-to-image generation, extending these techniques to controllable generation is still challenging. Existing controllable models, such as ControlNet, rely on dual-branch design that make distillation difficult. In this work, we adopt a simpler strategy. Instead of adding extra conditional branches, we finetune a selected subset of layers in the original text-to-image diffusion model to directly enable controllable generation. This results in DeltaControl, a single-flow, multi-step diffusion model capable of supporting spatial-condition generation while matching the performance of dual-branch approaches. Building on this teacher model, we further apply step-distillation to obtain FlashControl, a one-step model capable of spatial controllable generation with a single forward pass.

papers.title_en: GliomaINK: A Tumor and Anatomy Conditioned Flow Matching Framework for 3D MRI Sequence Synthesis in Glioma Patients
papers.authors: Moinak Bhattacharya, Annie Singh, Mohammad Chaudhry, Prateek Prasanna, Gagandeep Singh
papers.evidence: 解剖引导的条件流匹配用于三维医学体积合成
papers.tldr: 多参数MRI不完整会限制胶质瘤表征与下游AI分析。GliomaINK以解剖结构为条件、采用流匹配进行跨序列3D MRI合成，并用3D SwinUNETR预测速度场及拓扑保持损失约束结构。模型在1083例BraTS-AG训练、内部临床队列独立测试，六个转换方向PSNR均最高，T2W→T1C达25.64 dB；下游分割与IDH1预测表现强。该工作表明解剖引导条件流匹配可高保真合成胶质瘤MRI并保留临床相关信息。
papers.abstract_en: Background: Incomplete multiparametric MR examinations limit glioma characterization and downstream AI tools. Generative models can synthesize missing MRI sequences, but anatomical structure and clinically relevant tumor features are challenging to preserve. We propose GliomaINK, an anatomy-guided conditional flow matching framework for cross-sequence 3D brain MRI synthesis.   Methods: A 3D SwinUNETR predicted the conditional velocity field while an auxiliary topology-preserving loss encouraged structural consistency. The model was trained on 1,083 patients from the BraTS-AG dataset and independently tested on an in-house clinical cohort. Downstream tasks include image quality, tumor segmentation, IDH1 mutation-status prediction, and overall survival prediction. Two radiologists independently evaluated the anatomical fidelity, pathological representation, and overall image quality of the synthesized images.   Results: GliomaINK exhibited the highest PSNR across all six MRI translation directions in both evaluation cohorts. In the BraTS-AG test set, the PSNR reached $25.64\pm0.55$ dB for the T2W-to-T1C synthesis, compared with $13.78\pm0.32$ dB for Pix2Pix and $18.90\pm0.53$ dB for SPADE. For downstream tumor segmentation, the method showed strong performance across tumor subregions with Dice scores reaching $0.928\pm0.014$ for edema, and $0.885\pm0.040$ for enhancing tumor. For the IDH1 mutation-status prediction, GliomaINK achieved the highest AUROC score in four of the six sequence configurations, reaching $0.827\pm0.088$.   Conclusion: Anatomy-guided conditional flow matching enables high-fidelity cross-sequence glioma MRI synthesis demonstrating potential for preservation of clinically relevant information in synthesized MRI and improving downstream tasks.

papers.title_en: Local Manifold Attention for Recovery and Generation of Rare 3D Human Poses
papers.evidence: 动作序列中稀有三维人体姿态的恢复与生成
papers.tldr: 稀有3D人体姿态可能源于真实动作，也可能是估计误差，而参考库样本稀少使校正与生成都困难。作者提出圆柱流形注意力Transformer（CMAT），以几何与任务相关的邻域权重扩展局部流形拟合。Self-Action CMAT利用序列内可比窗口、邻域不平衡校正和时间依赖建模，并结合鲁棒时间正则进行运动恢复；Rarity-preserving CMAT在局部支撑下生成稀有姿态。实验显示恢复降低位置与加速度误差，生成在常见筛选下产出更多合格稀有姿态。
papers.abstract_en: A rare 3D human pose in a motion sequence may reflect either a genuine movement or an estimation error, making correction difficult when reference databases contain few comparable examples. We investigate whether local geometric structure can support the recovery and generation of rare configura- tions, using motion-capture sequences from AMASS, which unifies datasets through a common parametric human-body model, together with video-based pose estimates. We develop the cylindrical manifold attention transformer (CMAT), which extends local manifold fitting through geometry- and task- dependent neighborhood weights. For motion correction, Self-Action CMAT draws on comparable windows within a sequence, adjusts their contributions for neighborhood imbalance and temporal dependence, and integrates local geometry with robust temporal regularization. Experiments on perturbed and estimated motions show reductions in position and acceleration errors, with component analyses examining how weighting and temporal processing con- tribute to recovery. The controlled correction comparisons are exploratory and conditional on the selected motion-amplitude bound. For generation, Rarity-preserving CMAT explores locally supported configurations subject to independently calibrated rarity and separation from stored observations. Under common screening criteria, it achieves a higher yield of eligible rare poses than the evaluated generation baselines.

papers.title_en: Distribution-Based Regularization for Reward Fine-Tuning Diffusion and Flow Models
papers.authors: Romeo Passaro, Jeongjae Lee, Jong Chul Ye, Michael M. Bronstein, Yoshua Bengio, Alexander Tong, Danyal Rehman
papers.evidence: 对预训练扩散与流匹配模型的奖励微调
papers.tldr: 奖励微调能使扩散与流匹配模型适配下游目标，但激进优化常导致模式坍塌与分布漂移。现有反向KL正则以速度场ℓ2惩罚实现，只是间接约束采样动态，并未直接作用于生成分布。DFR将KL正则从期望奖励推广到模型分布的凸泛函，其第一变分给出依赖分布的逐样本奖励，可统一导出FD、MMD和DreamSim多样性等正则。文生图微调中，DFR峰值奖励匹配KL调参基线，多样性最高提升29%，漂移持平或更低。
papers.abstract_en: Reward fine-tuning is an effective way to adapt pretrained diffusion and flow-matching models to downstream objectives, but aggressive optimization often leads to mode collapse and distributional drift. Existing methods attempt to control this drift with reverse-KL regularization, implemented as an $\ell_2$ penalty on the velocity field; however, this functions by indirectly constraining sampling dynamics rather than directly acting on the generated distribution. To address this, we propose DFR (Distributional Functional Rewards), which augments the task reward with a distribution-dependent, per-sample reward that acts explicitly on the generated distribution. Formally, we generalize the KL-regularized objective from expected rewards, which are linear in the model's distribution, to convex functionals of it. The first variation of this objective defines an effective, distribution-dependent reward that directly penalizes deviation from the pretrained distribution. This formulation yields additive per-sample rewards for the Fréchet distance (FD), maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), and DreamSim diversity, recovering several recently proposed rewards as special cases. Across various text-to-image fine-tuning tasks, DFR matches the peak reward of KL-tuned baselines while increasing diversity by up to 29% at equal or lower drift.

papers.title_en: TokenFlow: Latent Token Rectified Flow Matching for 3D Point Cloud Generation
papers.evidence: 面向三维形状生成的层次化整流流匹配
papers.tldr: 3D点云生成需兼顾部件布局与表面细节并保持置换等变性，但现有潜变量模型常将整体形状压成单向量，削弱部件级结构。TokenFlow用一组潜token表示形状，在token上做rectified flow，并用条件flow生成点，通过交叉注意力以O(NM)聚合全局上下文。在ShapeNet上其MMD与覆盖率领先，1-NNA与最强基线相当；在ModelNet10线性评估取得最佳报告精度。表明潜token集合是有效的3D点云生成表示。
papers.abstract_en: 3D point clouds generation requires capturing both part-level layout and surface detail while preserving permutation equivariance. Existing latent generative models often encode an entire shape into a single vector, which limits their ability to retain part-level structure. We propose TokenFlow, a hierarchical flow matching framework that represents each shape as a set of latent tokens and couples a rectified flow over these tokens with a conditional flow over points. A bottleneck of $M \ll N$ learnable tokens aggregates global context through cross-attention at $O(NM)$ cost. On ShapeNet, TokenFlow achieves the best MMD and coverage across airplane, car, and chair, while obtaining 1-NNA comparable to the strongest baselines. On ModelNet, its learned latent set reaches the best reported linear-evaluation accuracy on ModelNet10. These results show that representing a shape as a set of latent tokens, aggregated at $O(NM)$ cost, provides an effective representation for 3D point cloud generation.
